shorts.title: What you will learn: Virtual functions
shorts.script: One call, many behaviours. Today we meet polymorphism. One call can do many different things, depending on the real object. A virtual function is chosen at run time, by the real type of the object. You can hold a Dog in an Animal pointer, and a call to speak still runs the Dog version. Write virtual in the base. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: What you will learn: Virtual functions.

shorts.title: Virtual functions in one minute
shorts.hook: A virtual function is chosen at run time
shorts.script: A virtual function is chosen at run time, by the real type of the object. You can hold a Dog in an Animal pointer, and a call to speak still runs the Dog version. Write virtual in the base. Write override in the derived class, so that the compiler checks your spelling. Think of a remote control. One button, and each TV does its own thing. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Virtual functions in one minute.

shorts.title: Inside the second program
shorts.hook: The vector holds pointers to Animal.
shorts.script: The vector holds pointers to Animal. One is a Dog. One is a Cat. The loop does not care which is which. It makes one call, and each animal does its own thing. The output is Woof, and then Meow. The program prints Woof, and then Meow. A virtual function is chosen by the real type, at run time. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Inside the second program.

shorts.title: Bug of the Day: A function that is not virtual
shorts.hook: Can you spot the bug in virtual functions?
shorts.script: Can you spot the bug in virtual functions? Bug of the Day. We call speak through an Animal pointer to a Dog. The program prints three dots, not Woof. Speak is not virtual, so the pointer type decides. Add virtual in the base, and override in Dog. Without virtual, the compiler picks the function by the pointer type, which is Animal. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Bug of the Day: A function that is not virtual.

shorts.title: Pun and challenge
shorts.hook: Can you add a Cow to the zoo in virtual functions?
shorts.script: Can you add a Cow to the zoo in virtual functions? Why did the virtual function get a promotion? It always knew who it really was. Add a class Cow to the zoo program. Its speak prints Moo. Add one cow to the vector. Write your answer in the comments. A virtual function is chosen by the real type, at run time. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Pun and challenge.
